newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sanyo to start long-distance phone service.
newsitem.headline: Sanyo to start long-distance phone service.

text.p: Sanyo Electric Co said on Tuesday that it would launch a long-distance phone service for corporate customers in January 1997 at rates 30 percent lower than those of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp.
Sanyo said it would use its own lines for the service.
As part of a major deregulation package announced early this year, companies owning private lines were allowed to connect both ends of their lines to public networks from November 1.

Sanyo said it would charge 98 yen per three minutes for calls of more than 100 km, compared with NTT's 140 yen for a comparable call. A Sanyo spokesman said the firm plans to introduce its own rate cuts when NTT implements its planned rate cuts in February.
Sanyo aims to acquire 100 corporate customers and to reach one billion yen worth of sales by 2000, he said.
Matsushita Electric Industrial Co and Mitsubishi Electric Co have said they will start long-distance phone services next year using their own private lines.
The deregulation also allows companies without their own phone networks to offer telecommunications services by leasing private lines and connecting them to public networks.
